At most, I’ll have a rare day where the heavy cloud lifts just a little, and the voice and those awful thoughts of being cursed will quiet down, but it never lasts more than a day before it all comes back.\n\nDoctor: Have you had any episodes of feeling significantly better for at least two months at any point in your life before this past year, or has this constant feeling of guilt and heaviness been a persistent issue with no prolonged periods of relief?\n\nPatient: Before this past year, I was actually doing completely fine and didn't feel this way at all. I used to really enjoy going to Zumba, hiking on the weekends, and being active at my church without any of this heaviness or guilt. But since all of this started about fourteen months ago, it's just been a constant struggle with no real relief.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced more than one episode of feeling significantly better for at least two months before this current period of constant guilt and heaviness, or was this the first time you've struggled with these feelings for an extended period?\n\nPatient: No, this is the first time I've ever gone through anything like this. Before I started pushing myself so hard with the GED and extra shifts about fourteen months ago, I was doing okay and keeping up with my church and Zumba. This past year has just been one long, continuous struggle without any breaks.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned this is the first time you've experienced such a long period of guilt and heaviness, but can you tell me if you've had any previous episodes of feeling down or depressed that lasted for more than two weeks but less than two months before this current episode started?\n\nPatient: I don't recall ever having a period of feeling down or depressed like this before this past year. I was usually busy but generally doing okay and staying active with my routines. This is definitely the first time I've ever struggled with these kinds of feelings.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned this is your first episode of feeling this way, but to clarify, have you had any periods of at least two weeks where you felt relatively normal or even happy since this constant feeling of guilt and heaviness started about fourteen months ago?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't had even two weeks of feeling normal or happy since this all started. It has just been one continuous dark period for over a year now. At most, I might get a single day where the heaviness lifts a tiny bit and the voice quiets down, but I never get a real break.\n\nDoctor: You've had this constant feeling of guilt and heaviness for over a year without any significant breaks, but can you tell me if you've experienced any changes in the intensity of these feelings over time, or have they remained relatively consistent?\n\nPatient: For the most part, the heavy, dark feeling has stayed really consistent and exhausting every single day. There are only very rare days when it lifts just a tiny bit, and on those days, the negative voices quiet down and the feeling of being cursed doesn't feel quite as strong. Otherwise, it has just been a continuous, heavy struggle that doesn't really change.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced significant changes in your sleep or appetite patterns since this constant feeling of guilt and heaviness started about fourteen months ago?\n\nPatient: My sleep has been absolutely terrible; I lie awake for hours replaying all my mistakes, and when I finally drift off, I wake up at 3 or 4 AM with my heart racing and can't get back to sleep. As for my appetite, I don't even have the energy to cook anymore, so my aunt has to bring me food, which just leaves me feeling completely exhausted and drained.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned enjoying activities like Zumba and hiking before this period started, but have you found any pleasure or interest in these or other activities since the heavy feeling and guilt began?\n\nPatient: No, I don't find any pleasure in them anymore. Things I used to love, like Zumba or helping at the youth center, just feel completely pointless and far away now. It's like I'm watching my life from under water.\n\nDoctor: You've described this as your first episode of feeling this way, lasting over a year without significant relief, but can you confirm if you've had any shorter periods of feeling down or depressed before this that might have lasted less than two weeks?\n\nPatient: No, I don't recall having any short periods of feeling down or depressed like this before this past year started. I was always pretty active and doing okay back then.\n\nDoctor: To confirm, you're saying that this is your first episode of depression, and it has lasted for more than two weeks, correct?\n\nPatient: Yes, that's correct. This is the first time I've ever felt like this, and it has been going on for a little over a year now, not just a couple of weeks. It all started back when I began pushing myself so hard with my GED and the extra work shifts.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned you no longer find pleasure in activities like Zumba or helping at the youth center, but have you completely lost interest in all activities you once enjoyed, or are there any that still bring you some small amount of joy or satisfaction?\n\nPatient: Yes, I have completely lost interest in everything, and absolutely nothing brings me joy anymore. Even the things I used to love just feel pointless and so far away now. It really feels like I'm just watching my life happen from underwater.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if there was a specific point or event when your feelings of guilt and heaviness started to become constant, or was it a gradual process over several months?\n\nPatient: It was definitely a gradual process that built up over about fourteen months. It started when I began pushing myself really hard to finish my GED while juggling all those extra work shifts, and it just slowly got worse over time. As I lost my routines and fell behind in school, the heaviness and guilt just kept growing until it became constant.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had thoughts of harming yourself or wished you were dead since this heavy feeling and guilt started?\n\nPatient: Yes, almost every day I catch myself thinking it would be better if I just didn’t wake up, since I feel like such a burden to everyone. On my worst nights, I've sat on my bed holding my old pain pills, planning out how many it would take to finally end things.\n\nDoctor: You've described a continuous period of guilt and heaviness for over a year without significant relief, but can you clarify if there have been any fluctuations in the severity of your symptoms during this time, such as periods where the feelings of guilt were slightly less intense?\n\nPatient: There are very rare days when the dark cloud lifts just a little bit and the heavy guilt isn't quite as strong. On those days, the feeling that God has cursed me fades slightly and the voice in my ear quiets down. But it never lasts more than a day before it all comes right back.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever acted on those thoughts of harming yourself or have a specific plan in place to end your life, or are they just recurring thoughts?\n\nPatient: I haven't actually taken them, but I still think about wishing I wouldn't wake up almost every single day. I also truly believe that because of my mistakes with my GED and at work, God has marked me as cursed. It tells me I'm worthless, that I've disappointed God, and that something terrible is going to happen to my family. I don't see anything that isn't there, but hearing him is so incredibly real and terrifying.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any other unusual perceptions, such as seeing or smelling things that others can't, in addition to hearing the voice?\n\nPatient: No, I don't see or smell anything unusual that isn't really there. The experience is completely limited to hearing that man's voice whispering behind my left ear when I'm alone.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about what you mean by 'God has marked me as cursed' and if you believe this is a fact or just a feeling you have?\n\nPatient: I know it sounds crazy to others, but I am deeply convinced it's a fact that God has cursed me because of my failures with school and work. On the rare days when my depression lifts slightly, the thought fades, but when I'm really low, it feels entirely like a fact.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any other hallucinations, such as seeing things that aren't there, in addition to hearing the voice behind your left ear?"

Otherwise, it has just been a continuous, heavy struggle that doesn't really change.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced significant changes in your sleep or appetite patterns since this constant feeling of guilt and heaviness started about fourteen months ago?\n\nPatient: My sleep has been absolutely terrible; I lie awake for hours replaying all my mistakes, and when I finally drift off, I wake up at 3 or 4 AM with my heart racing and can't get back to sleep. As for my appetite, I don't even have the energy to cook anymore, so my aunt has to bring me food, which just leaves me feeling completely exhausted and drained.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned enjoying activities like Zumba and hiking before this period started, but have you found any pleasure or interest in these or other activities since the heavy feeling and guilt began?\n\nPatient: No, I don't find any pleasure in them anymore. Things I used to love, like Zumba or helping at the youth center, just feel completely pointless and far away now. It's like I'm watching my life from under water.\n\nDoctor: You've described this as your first episode of feeling this way, lasting over a year without significant relief, but can you confirm if you've had any shorter periods of feeling down or depressed before this that might have lasted less than two weeks?\n\nPatient: No, I don't recall having any short periods of feeling down or depressed like this before this past year started. I was always pretty active and doing okay back then.\n\nDoctor: To confirm, you're saying that this is your first episode of depression, and it has lasted for more than two weeks, correct?\n\nPatient: Yes, that's correct. This is the first time I've ever felt like this, and it has been going on for a little over a year now, not just a couple of weeks. It all started back when I began pushing myself so hard with my GED and the extra work shifts.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned you no longer find pleasure in activities like Zumba or helping at the youth center, but have you completely lost interest in all activities you once enjoyed, or are there any that still bring you some small amount of joy or satisfaction?\n\nPatient: Yes, I have completely lost interest in everything, and absolutely nothing brings me joy anymore. Even the things I used to love just feel pointless and so far away now. It really feels like I'm just watching my life happen from underwater.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if there was a specific point or event when your feelings of guilt and heaviness started to become constant, or was it a gradual process over several months?\n\nPatient: It was definitely a gradual process that built up over about fourteen months. It started when I began pushing myself really hard to finish my GED while juggling all those extra work shifts, and it just slowly got worse over time. As I lost my routines and fell behind in school, the heaviness and guilt just kept growing until it became constant.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had thoughts of harming yourself or wished you were dead since this heavy feeling and guilt started?\n\nPatient: Yes, almost every day I catch myself thinking it would be better if I just didn’t wake up, since I feel like such a burden to everyone. On my worst nights, I've sat on my bed holding my old pain pills, planning out how many it would take to finally end things.\n\nDoctor: You've described a continuous period of guilt and heaviness for over a year without significant relief, but can you clarify if there have been any fluctuations in the severity of your symptoms during this time, such as periods where the feelings of guilt were slightly less intense?\n\nPatient: There are very rare days when the dark cloud lifts just a little bit and the heavy guilt isn't quite as strong. On those days, the feeling that God has cursed me fades slightly and the voice in my ear quiets down.
